title: What Networked Players is — and isn't, yet.
lede: An evidence-first music-credit graph and game. Given two artists or releases, it presents a documented route through credited work and explains each step.

sections.heading: The idea
paragraphs: Release credits document who played, produced, engineered, arranged, or sang on a record. Networked Players treats those credits as a graph: two artists are connected when they're credited on the same release or track, and a path between two artists is a chain of those connections.
The point is the evidence. Every hop in a path keeps its proof attached — the release, the role text, the credit scope — so you can see exactly why two artists are linked.

sections.heading: Evidence, not influence
paragraphs: A shared credit proves participation — that two artists are credited on the same release. It doesn't prove they influenced each other, that they were friends, or that any artistic lineage exists between them. This site only shows what the credits themselves say, nothing it has to guess at.

sections.heading: Where the project actually is
paragraphs: The album grid and evidence viewer run on Discogs monthly-dump data (snapshot 20260601): {{studioAlbumCount}} studio albums, {{artistCount}} artists, {{documentedConnectionCount}} documented connections, drawn from a bounded working set seeded by a private collection that's never itself published. Album years are the master's original release year, and the catalog excludes live albums, soundtracks, compilations, and other non-studio releases by default.

The flagship Connection Guesser game (below) runs on the same catalog: {{oneHopRoundCount}} one-hop and {{twoHopRoundCount}} two-hop rounds derived from those {{studioAlbumCount}} studio albums and their credits. (An earlier synthetic round set still exists as a test fixture, but nobody plays it.) Connection of the Day serves one frozen round per local calendar day from a committed schedule. Record Routes is a third mode on the same catalog: guess how many credited hops connect two records, and, for two-hop routes, who bridges them.

The connections demo on this site runs separately, on a small, curated subset of Discogs releases and artist connections — fetched via the Discogs API ahead of the full CC0 dump pipeline (see the project's ADR 0012).

sections.heading: Data and rights
paragraphs: Publishable catalog facts derive from CC0 Discogs monthly data dumps, always carried with provenance: snapshot date, source URL, parser and schema versions, and the original role text.

Private collection membership is never published, and raw API responses stay on the coordination host. The demo dataset here is fetched from the private seed's release list but curated down to a small subset — deliberately too small a fraction to reconstruct real collection membership. Cover art is hotlinked directly from Discogs' own CDN, never downloaded or rehosted; marketplace and pricing data remain out of scope entirely.

sections.heading: What's shipped since Phase 1
paragraphs: A first-class role taxonomy for credits (producer, engineer, performer, and more, alongside the original role text), a searchable contributors directory that makes the people behind these records as navigable as the albums themselves, and a real record-to-record search — Connect Two Records — over every credited contributor on any two catalog albums, not just their primary artists. Explore adds an open-ended, bounded network view of one album's documented credit neighborhood, and three role-restricted search modes (Behind the Glass, Rhythm Section, Guitar Paths) narrow a search to a specific kind of credit.

Every one of those surfaces now links directly into the others: an album page opens straight into Connect (pre-filled) or Explore (centered on the album's own artist); a contributor page opens Explore centered on that person specifically; Explore's current center links back to its own contributor page when one exists; and every documented evidence hop, in both Connect and Explore, links each credited name to their own contributor page. The site stays one connected graph to move through, page to page.

sections.heading: What's next
paragraphs: The connections demo still runs on its original API-sourced dataset; replacing it with one derived from the CC0 monthly dumps, with full provenance and no collection membership, hasn't happened yet. A future live-search mode would only ever add to the site — the static-first core keeps working on its own either way.
